target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw cron run` (a manual/operator run) on a `deleteAfterRun` one-shot ("at") job used to delete the job on success — consuming the one-shot so its scheduled fire never happened (issue #83538). Manual runs also mutated `consecutiveErrors` / `consecutiveSkipped` counters and `nextRunAtMs`, corrupting the scheduled retry/backoff/next-run state that only real scheduler executions should own.

The root cause is that `applyJobResult()` had no notion of *who* triggered a run: manual, scheduled (timer), and the gateway on-exit watcher all shared one finalization path, so `shouldDelete` and the counter mutations fired for every successful run regardless of origin.

## Why This Change Was Made

Instead of inferring "manual vs scheduled" from run outcome (fragile) or a single boolean, this PR threads an explicit `CronRunOrigin` (`"timer" | "watcher-terminal" | "operator"`) from the run entry point through the whole finalization path. Origin is the accurate ownership model:

- `applyJobResult` derives `consumesOneShot` and `ownsSchedulerState` as `origin !== "operator"`, and records `lastRunWasManual = origin === "operator"`.
- Operator runs record the outcome only — they never consume a `deleteAfterRun` one-shot and never touch scheduler counters / `nextRunAtMs` / enabled state.
- `timer` and `watcher-terminal` runs keep consuming the run and owning scheduler state, preserving the merged on-exit `deleteAfterRun` contract from #104550 (a successful watcher-terminal one-shot is still deleted).

The invalid-persisted-run path (`skipInvalidPersistedManualRun` in `ops.ts`) previously hard-coded `origin: "operator"`. Because the gateway on-exit watcher reaches that path with `origin: "watcher-terminal"`, an invalid persisted watcher run was mis-attributed as operator, diverging scheduler-owned counters/alerts/terminal state from other watcher executions. The caller origin is now forwarded through preflight into that finalization so every path carries the true origin.

## User Impact

- Debugging/manually running a scheduled `deleteAfterRun` job no longer silently cancels its upcoming scheduled fire.
- Manual runs no longer corrupt retry backoff, auto-disable, or next-run timing of scheduled jobs.
- Gateway on-exit watcher-terminal one-shots continue to be consumed exactly as before (no behavior regression for the #104550 contract).
- Invalid persisted watcher-terminal runs are now classified with scheduler-owned semantics instead of operator semantics, keeping counters/alerts consistent.

## Evidence

Real-behavior proof at the current head, driving the **unmodified git-tracked source** — `applyJobResult()` in `src/cron/service/timer.ts` and the store mutation in `applyOutcomeToStoredJob()` — through all three origins on a `deleteAfterRun` one-shot. Run inside a `node:24-bookworm-slim` container (container node v24.18.0, the supported runtime floor is 24.15.0) with the repo's own vitest, and corroborated by the committed regression suite.

```
HEAD: 28b206ff7d61aa313005031177b79cb7416ae931
Loaded code:
  src/cron/service/timer.ts :: applyJobResult()
    consumesOneShot    = origin !== "operator"
    ownsSchedulerState = origin !== "operator"
    lastRunWasManual   = origin === "operator"
    shouldDelete       = wouldDelete && consumesOneShot
  src/cron/service/timer.ts :: applyOutcomeToStoredJob()
    if (shouldDelete) store.jobs = jobs.filter(e => e.id !== job.id)
  src/cron/service/ops.ts   :: skipInvalidPersistedManualRun()
    applyJobResult(..., { origin: params.origin })   // caller origin forwarded

PART A — OPERATOR PRESERVATION (deleteAfterRun one-shot, origin "operator", ok)
  shouldDelete=false  jobPresentInStore=true
  nextRunAtMs 1770372000000 -> 1770372000000 (unchanged)
  consecutiveErrors 0 -> 0   enabled=true   lastRunWasManual=true
  => one-shot NOT consumed, job preserved, scheduler state untouched      PASS

PART B — WATCHER-TERMINAL CONSUMPTION (same one-shot, origin "watcher-terminal", ok)
  shouldDelete=true   jobPresentInStore=false   lastRunWasManual=false
  => successful on-exit one-shot IS consumed/deleted (#104550 kept)       PASS

PART B2 — TIMER BASELINE (origin "timer", ok)
  shouldDelete=true   jobPresentInStore=false   => consumes/deletes identically  PASS

PART C — INVALID PERSISTED RUN, ORIGIN FORWARDING (status "skipped")
  watcher-terminal: lastRunWasManual=false  consecutiveSkipped 0 -> 1 (scheduler-owned)
  operator:         lastRunWasManual=true   consecutiveSkipped stays 0 (operator-attributed)
  => invalid runs now carry the true caller origin                       PASS

Harness result (container node v24.18.0, vitest 4.1.9): 4 passed (4)
Committed regression suite src/cron/service/ops.regression.test.ts: 21 passed (21)
OVERALL: PASS
```

The regression suite adds parametrized coverage asserting watcher-terminal invalid runs keep scheduled/consuming scheduler-state semantics while operator invalid runs stay operator-attributed.
